chunks: 1. Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr and Zurārah, the two sons of Aʿyan, that they asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the wudu (ablution) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, so he called for a basin or a vessel in which there was...

water. Then he washed his two hands, then dipped his right hand into the vessel and washed his face with it, and he used his left hand with his palm to help in washing his face. Then he dipped his right hand into the water and scooped water with it, and washed his right hand from the elbow to the fingers, not returning the water to the two elbows. Then he dipped his right hand into the water and scooped with it from the water, then poured it over his left hand from the elbow to the palm, not returning the water to the elbow, just as he did with the right. Then he wiped his head and his feet up to the ankles with the moisture remaining on his two palms; he did not renew water.
2. As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-ʿAbbās, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

There is no problem with wiping in wudu (ablution) forwards and backwards. So this report is specific to wiping the two feet, because it is permissible to wipe them in a forward direction and in a backward direction. That which indicates this is:

3. What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, who said: Someone who saw Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام at Minā informed me...
that he was wiping the top of his two feet from the upper part of the foot to the ankle, and from the ankle to the upper part of the foot.

key_terms.الْكَعْبَيْنِ: the two ankles, the limit mentioned for wiping the feet
key_terms.الْمِرْفَقِ: the elbow, the starting point for washing the arm
key_terms.بِفَضْلِ كَفَّيْهِ: with the remaining moisture of his two palms, without renewing water
key_terms.ظَهْرَ قَدَمَيْهِ: the top of his two feet, the place being wiped
key_terms.غَسَلَ: he washed, referring to the washing acts in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.مَسَحَ: he wiped, referring to wiping the head and feet
key_terms.مُقْبِلًا وَمُدْبِرًا: forwards and backwards, describing the direction of wiping
key_terms.وُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification being described

ai.seo_question: How is wudu (ablution) performed, and can the feet be wiped in both directions?
ai.summary: This report describes the manner of wudu (ablution), including washing the face and arms and wiping the head and feet with the remaining moisture on the hands without taking new water. It also cites a report permitting wiping in both directions, and explains that this applies specifically to wiping the feet.
